title: Encoding review: how each implication case is encoded for the omega (LIA) decision

variable_domain.evidence: closure_complete.py:93-96,108 — lean_theorem declares `(v_<name> : Int)`; _goal_statement binds `∀ (v_... : Int)`.
variable_domain.note: The restricted view (used by the matrix) carries ONLY these 11 base integer variables. Encoding over Int (not Nat) is deliberate: it lets omega see e.g. n-1, m-(n-1) without an implicit >=0 wrap; the required lower bounds are supplied EXPLICITLY (below), so nothing nonnegative is left implicit.

nonnegativity.claim: In the RESTRICTED encoding every variable that appears is one of the 11 base invariants, and EACH carries an explicit nonneg fact v>=0, plus stronger lower bounds where a property licenses them. No nonnegative invariant is left without its constraint.

nonneg_facts.src: deduction.py:122-125 — for v in NONNEG_VARS: inv.append(nonneg_<v>: {v:1} >= 0)

product_variables.justification: These are NONLINEAR (products). The RESTRICTED view used by the matrix clears PRODUCT_FACTS entirely (_restricted_inventory), so NO product variable appears in the restricted omega encoding. Therefore the 'missing nonneg for a product var' risk does not arise in the matrix encoding. (In the non-restricted/product view they are nonnegative by construction as products of nonnegative base invariants; they are introduced only by the product identity facts that define them.)

inventory_constraints.linearity: All restricted inventory facts are linear over the 11 base invariants (no products). Confirmed: closure_complete.py:11-12 ('the restricted view carries no product terms'); active_restricted_facts iterates G.DED.INVENTORY under _restricted_inventory.

rational_to_integer_scaling.mechanism: For each deducer Fact (coeffs are Fraction, const is Fraction), L = lcm of all denominators (coeffs + const); multiply through by L (positive); emit integer `coeffs·x REL -const`.
rational_to_integer_scaling.soundness: L>0 always (lcm of positive denominators). Multiplying `A REL 0` by L>0 preserves REL for REL in {>=,==} (the only rels emitted: rel is '==' if f.rel=='==' else '>='). The result is EQUIVALENT (not merely sound) because L>0 is invertible over the rationals; omega then decides over Z. No rounding is applied in scaling (unlike canon's tightening).
rational_to_integer_scaling.exactness: Only Fraction/int arithmetic; no float anywhere in the scaling or the omega decision.

floors_ceilings.where: canon.py:52-54 — for '>=' facts, gcd-reduce coefficients and replace const by floor(const//g) (Python floor division, also for negatives).
floors_ceilings.soundness: Integer tightening: (g·c)·x + const >= 0 with integer x is equivalent to c·x + ceil(const/g)/... ; for '>=' the floor of const/g is the tightest integer bound that all integer solutions satisfy — sound and complete over Z. Example: 2x-3>=0 -> x-2>=0; 2x+3>=0 -> x+1>=0.
floors_ceilings.scope: canon.py tightening is applied to the CONTENT KEY / proposition canonicalisation, not inside closure_complete's LCM scaling (which uses exact multiplication). The omega decision receives integer constraints and decides over Z, so floors are not needed at decision time.
floors_ceilings.equality_unsat: canon.py: for '==' facts, if gcd does not divide const the constraint is UNSATISFIABLE -> FALSE (sound).

list.turan_r2..r6: omega <= r  =>  2r*m <= (r-1)*N2  (Mantel/Turan; involves product N2 — product view only)

conditional_theorems.firing: collect_facts_complete iterates conditionals to a FIXPOINT: a conditional fires iff omega proves its hypothesis from the current fact set (closure_complete.py:248-259). In the RESTRICTED matrix view only conditionals whose hypothesis AND conclusion are product-free survive (e.g. complete_indep).

property_lattice.exclusive: has_cycle <=> not is_acyclic; is_bipartite <=> chi<=2; not_bipartite <=> chi>=3

parametric.is_regular(d): exact match only (is_regular(2) does NOT discharge is_regular(3)); emits 2m = d*n (product view)
parametric.is_k_edge_connected(k): monotone: k'-edge-connected discharges k iff k' >= k; emits min_deg >= k
parametric.decision: pf_trust.props.dischargeable (parametric properties never passed to the non-parametric lattice closure)

two_sided_guarantee.PROVEN: Lean certificate = the batch proof (B1-B7): theorem over Int with omega, axioms ⊆ {propext,Classical.choice,Quot.sound}. Cross-check (C4): z3 integer solver must find (facts ∧ ¬goal) UNSAT.
two_sided_guarantee.NOT_PROVEN: z3 integer solver must find a concrete INTEGER witness where every fact holds and the goal fails (C3); the witness is re-checked in pure Python with Fraction (pf_trust.certify.recheck_witness).
two_sided_guarantee.disagreement_policy: z3 (complete for LIA) and omega (complete for LIA) must agree on every linear-integer case. Any disagreement is surfaced, not hidden, and investigated as an encoding bug / missing constraint / out-of-fragment case.
